newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Women's democracy-building forum begins in Vienna.
newsitem.headline: Women's democracy-building forum begins in Vienna.

text.p: Hundreds of high-profile women from the United States and Europe arrived on Wednesday for a forum on strengthening the role of women in the new democracies of former Eastern bloc countries.
U.S. Ambassador to Austria Swanee Hunt opened the three-day gathering in Vienna, entitled "Vital Voices: Women in Democracy". It will be addressed by U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton on Friday.

"The voices of women are vitally important for the creation of democracy," said Hunt, chairing and sponsoring the forum. She is also a major financial contributor to President Bill Clinton's election campaigns.

Maria Rauch-Kallat, General Secretary of the Austrian People's Party, welcomed more than 300 delegates and said she hoped the forum would be a good opportunity for network-building and exchanging ideas.
Delegates will participate in workshops exploring leadership strategies in law, politics and business.

The group included European Union Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs Emma Bonino, National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz, Czech Senate Vice-President Jaroslava Moserova, and former Lithuanian prime minister Kazimiera Prunskiene.
